messages:
morgan: FYI seeing a spike in p95 after the kernel-selector pruning merged last night. Canary shows prefill-heavy requests tailing out, and decode short flows are getting delayed.
alex: which PR/commit? paste link.
morgan: 0f9c8b2 — kernel prune + bias to small batched kernels. Repro on canary with a mixed workload (long prefill 50% / short decode 50%).
chloe: can you drop the perf snapshot? p50/p95, tok/s?
morgan: sure:
``
canary @2x load
baseline v3.2.0:
  p50 45ms, p95 120ms, tok/s 18k
post-prune v3.2.1:
  p50 48ms, p95 215ms, tok/s 17.2k
prefill-heavy flows p95 ~300ms
decode-short flows p95 ~280ms
KV fill latencies higher, kernel threads skewed
```
alex: ouch. sounds like prefill batches are growing and starving decode. Any profiler/flames?
ben: grabbed a flame from the canary — pattern: batch_wait -> kernel_dispatch -> kv_get (miss) -> kernel_fallback_hotloop. KV miss penalty ~8-12ms per get, accumulates when prefill batches are large.
morgan: that matches what I see. Proposed mitigations: (A) enforce queue phase-split so prefill vs decode don't mix; (B) add a short decode-preemption/handshake window so decode can cut in; (C) kernel-routing change to reduce KV churn for prefill.
chloe: what's the smallest change to get tail down?
ben: phase-split + tiny decode reservation works fast. I ran an experiment locally with explicit token targets and a 6ms handshake; decode p95 dropped ~45%. Prefill p95 slightly up but overall tail improved.
ben: experiment config:
``
batcher.phase_split = true
batcher.prefill_tokens_target = 256
batcher.decode_tokens_target = 64
scheduler.handshake_window_ms = 6
kernel.selector.decode_bias = 0.7
```
ben: KV-hit-by-phase improved — decode hit rate +11% because smaller decode batches map to warmer KV sets. Throughput dip ~2% but effective TPS for production unchanged due to tail reduction.
alex: good. Longer-term: teach kernel selector to use phase-aware signals: prefer KV-friendly kernels for prefill, low-latency kernels for decode. Also add max-wait-per-batch-ms and soft wait-steal: if prefill batch wait > N ms, allow decode to steal streams.
morgan: agreed. I'll add a reproducible perf job with the mixed-length synthetic to perf-jobs and attach flames. ben: please also add a metric batch_phase_mix (ratio of prefill streams in a batch) and kv_hit_rate_by_phase — super useful for diagnosing mixed batches.
chloe: can someone own the scheduler patch? handshake window + max-wait seems small.
alex: I'll take the scheduler handshake + max-wait patch. Ben will evolve kernel selector heuristics. Morgan will create the perf job.
perf-bot: deploy-canary started: alex/phase-handshake-waitsteal @ canary-42
oncall: noted. watching canary dashboards and paging thresholds.
morgan: timeline: 1) small canary with phase split + handshake window (today) 2) collect batch_phase_mix & kv_hit_by_phase (48h) 3) expand canaries if good, then gradual prod rollout 4) follow-up RFC for kernel selector phase signals before next sprint.
chloe: also add dashboards for max-batch-wait and per-kernel-kv-churn so we can correlate.
alex: we'll keep the default off for now and gate by a feature-flag. If canary looks clean we flip for non-critical clusters first.
ben: FYI in the kernel selector work, avoid a hard bias that reduces kernel diversity — the right move is a small phase-weight that nudges selection, plus a tie-breaker on per-kernel kv-churn metric.
morgan: job created: perf-job/7864, attaching flame + tarball when finished. Will post a short summary with before/after numbers.
chloe: thanks — sounds like a solid path.
alex: action items: alex -> scheduler patch (handshake + max-wait + reservation), ben -> kernel selector phase-add, morgan -> perf-job + artifacts, chloe -> add dashboard tiles and KV-by-phase metrics. oncall -> monitor.
perf-bot: canary metrics telemetry: initial p95 moving target appended to dashboard.
oncall: will alert on regressions above 20% of baseline p95.
morgan: will update thread with artifacts + final verdict once canary finishes.
